analysis.title: Global Semiconductors 2027E Global Memory Supply & Demand Projection: DRAM S/D Ratio at -3.8%, NAND S/D Ratio at -3.3%
key_insights: Citi narrows its 2027E DRAM supply/demand ratio to -3.8% from -8.7% and its NAND ratio to -3.3% from -6.1%, reflecting higher bit growth guidance from Samsung and SK Hynix in 3Q26 earnings and weaker consumer NAND demand.

2027E DRAM supply growth is +24% versus demand growth of +28%. Citi's prior estimates were +19% supply and +30% demand. Demand growth was trimmed because handset DRAM demand is expected to fall 11% YoY.
Citi projects Samsung 2027E DRAM bit supply +22% and SK Hynix +28%, with the Hynix increase driven by the 1cnm capacity ramp.
Server DRAM demand is forecast to grow 53% YoY in 2027E and eSSD demand 52% YoY, supported by a 38% YoY rise in content per box. These are the main drivers keeping demand ahead of incremental supply.

2027E NAND supply growth is +22% versus demand growth of +26%. Prior estimates were +21% supply and +29% demand. Suppliers are using node migration to meet eSSD demand, and consumer NAND demand is weaker than Citi expected.
Citi raises its 2027E DRAM capex growth estimate to +55% YoY from +52% and NAND capex growth to +35% from +34%. For 2028E it projects DRAM capex +52% and NAND capex +34%.
Citi still expects memory undersupply in 2027E despite the higher supply guidance. The current supply/demand fulfillment ratio is about 70%.

Citi says memory suppliers are not seeking excessive price increases and are pursuing mid-to-long-term earnings visibility through long-term agreements (LTAs), which it believes supports continued undersupply.
Citi addresses market concern over higher-than-expected 4Q bit supply growth at Samsung and SK Hynix and argues demand growth still outpaces incremental supply.
Over the mid-to-long term, Citi expects continual learning and potential emergence of personal AI to keep driving memory demand.

market_movers.rationale: Target is about 8x C27E EPS, a slight premium to prior DRAM upturn trading ranges given an unprecedented pricing environment and the emergence of SCAs. Shares were $833.59 at the 02 Nov close.
Valued at 7-8x CY27E EPS versus Kioxia at a median 8x and peers at 6-8x. Citi says Sandisk's LTAs merit the higher range and that it has no DRAM exposure. Shares were $1,075.08 at the 02 Nov close.
Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) target uses SOTP on 2026E EBITDA, with a 5.9x multiple for Memory. Shares were W219,500.
SK Hynix (000660.KS) target uses SOTP on 2026E EBITDA, with 7.9x EV/EBITDA for HBM and 6.3x for commodity memory. Shares were W1,398,000.
Kioxia Holdings (285A.T) target applies 8.0x fair-value P/E to FY3/28E EPS of ¥5,448. Rated High Risk. Shares were ¥11,345.

Target is 25x 2027E EPS, above its three-year average forward P/E, justified by leading advanced-node position and AI demand outlook. Equates to about 36x 2026E and 25x 2027E P/E. Shares were NT$2,295.

sector_views.rationale: Demand growth still outpaces supply growth in 2027E for both DRAM and NAND, with server DRAM and eSSD demand leading and a supply/demand fulfillment ratio near 70%.

earnings_insights: Citi revised its memory supply/demand estimates after 3Q26 earnings calls from Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, which raised bit growth guidance.

Citi's valuation basis for Micron is about 8x C27E EPS (estimate), and for Sandisk 7-8x CY27E EPS (estimate). Kioxia uses FY3/28E EPS of ¥5,448 (Citi estimate, common stock before just under 1% dilution).
Kioxia sensitivity: Citi estimates each ¥1 of yen appreciation erodes operating profit by about ¥55bn.
risk_factors: Higher-than-expected 4Q bit supply growth at Samsung and SK Hynix is a market concern, though Citi expects shortage to persist.
Excess DRAM or NAND bits shipped into the channel could cause inventory reduction and lower pricing (Micron risk).
A competitor cutting DRAM or NAND prices, or adding capacity, could lower pricing and create excess bit supply if demand fails to materialize.
Kioxia: US relaxation of export restrictions on chip equipment to China, expanded industry investment, temporary smartphone and data center inventory adjustments, and yen strength.
Sandisk: slower Enterprise share gains, macro weakness hitting datacenter spend, PC refresh and AI-PC traction, and pricing volatility from supply-demand imbalance.
Samsung: delayed HBM shipment approval at key customers, weaker PC and NAND demand, aggressive competitor investment, handset competition and won appreciation.
SK Hynix: a downturn in DRAM demand, weaker NAND demand and weak global consumption.

TSMC: weak global semiconductor market, margin contraction from depreciation and strong NTD, new foundry competitors, longer inventory digestion, and a demand slowdown from economic downturn or tariff-driven trade disruption.
charts_described: Figure 1 shows the DRAM supply/demand outlook with a 2027E S/D ratio of -3.8%. Figure 2 shows the NAND supply/demand outlook with a 2027E S/D ratio of -3.3%. Figure 3 shows DRAM/NAND capex projections.
geopolitical: Citi lists a deterioration in memory supply-demand if the US relaxes restrictions on exports of semiconductor production equipment to China as a risk to Kioxia's target price.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand growth of +28% DRAM and +26% NAND still outpaces supply growth of +24% and +22%, with server DRAM +53% and eSSD +52%, a fulfillment ratio near 70%, and suppliers using LTAs rather than seeking excessive price increases.
tension_points.bear_case: Samsung and SK Hynix raised bit growth guidance (Samsung +22%, Hynix +28%), and market concern exists over higher 4Q bit supply. Consumer NAND and handset DRAM demand are weakening, and capex is rising (DRAM +55%, NAND +35%).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Excess DRAM or NAND bits shipped into the channel causing inventory reduction and lower pricing, or a competitor lowering DRAM or NAND pricing.

theme_stances.key_argument: Demand growth continues to outpace incremental supply growth, so memory undersupply persists despite higher supplier bit guidance.
theme_stances.evidence: We foresee continued memory undersupply in 2027E.
